title: Bound for a squared Gaussian score
statement: Let $I$ be finite, let $v\ge0$, and let $c,z,a\in\mathbb R^I$ satisfy $a_i\ge0$, $p_v(c_i,z_i)\le a_i$, and $\left|\left((z_i-c_i)^2/v^2-1/v\right)p_v(c_i,z_i)\right|\le a_i$ for every $i\in I$, where $p_v(u,w)$ denotes the Gaussian density with mean $u$ and variance $v$. Then for each $i\in I$, $\frac{(z_i-c_i)^2}{v^2}\prod_{j\in I}p_v(c_j,z_j)\le(1+1/v)\prod_{j\in I}a_j$.
hypotheses_covered: The conclusion holds for each $i\in I$
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Write $p_v(c,z)$ for the $N(c,v)$ density when $v>0$ and set $p_0(c,z)=0$; define $G_v(c,z)=\prod_{i\in I}p_v(c_i,z_i)$ and interpret division by zero as zero. Assume $c,z,a\in\mathbb R^I$, $a_i\ge0$, $p_v(c_i,z_i)\le a_i$, and $|((z_i-c_i)^2/v^2-1/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)|\le a_i$ for every $i\in I$. For every $i\in I$, $((z_i-c_i)^2/v^2)G_v(c,z)\le(1+1/v)\prod_j a_j$.
